You are a careful, neutral coder of the STRUCTURE OF A CORPORATE TRANSACTION AT
CLOSING. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from public primary sources
(SEC filings, company releases, reputable press). This slice describes ONLY how the
deal was structured -- what crossed the ownership boundary and what did not -- at
the moment of closing. You are DELIBERATELY NOT shown what happened to the combined
company afterward, and you must NOT speculate about later outcomes, success, or
failure. Code STRICTLY the deal as structured. If the slice does not let you
determine a field, you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from
outside knowledge of the companies.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

A. BUNDLE SIGNATURE -- for each of six organizational tiers, classify what happened
to that tier when the transaction crossed the ownership boundary. Exactly one label
per tier.
  T1 Owner Intent (controlling principal / imprint).
     Labels: replace, imprint-share, continue, terminate, reconstruct, replicate, mutual-replace, uncertain.
       replace = old controlling intent exited, a new one installed;
       imprint-share = both principals' intent co-present;
       continue = same controlling intent persists;
       terminate = the controlling intent ended with no successor;
       reconstruct = intent re-formed into a new (often non-commercial) purpose;
       replicate = intent copied into a standardized template (e.g. franchising);
       mutual-replace = two intents fused into a jointly-new one (merger of equals).
  T2 Business Model, T3 Business Entity (legal vehicle), T4 Product (customer-
  acceptance layer), T5 Process (operations), T6 Organization (people/culture).
     Labels for T2-T6: 1-1, N-1, 1-N, subset, partial, read-only, swap, terminate, null, uncertain.
       1-1 = transferred whole, one-to-one; N-1 = many collapsed into one;
       1-N = one split into many; subset = only part transferred;
       partial = transferred but incompletely / with friction;
       read-only = licensed / accessed without ownership transfer;
       swap = exchanged for a different one (e.g. new legal domicile);
       terminate = ended; null = not applicable / nothing at this tier.

B. TIER-TRANSFER GAPS -- code strictly from the STRUCTURE OF THE DEAL AT CLOSING.
A gap is a STRUCTURAL MISMATCH IN WHAT THE DEAL TRANSFERRED, not a later failure.
  gap_45: Did the customer-facing product/asset (T4, what customers buy) cross the
    ownership boundary WITHOUT the operational processes that produce or deliver it
    (T5) transferring or being aligned coherently alongside it? A documented
    product-vs-process structural mismatch AT CLOSING. 1 = yes such a gap; 0 = no
    (product and its processes moved together, or neither moved); uncertain.
  gap_56: Did the operational processes (T5) transfer or get re-engineered WITHOUT
    the organization / people / management / culture that run them (T6) transferring
    or aligning coherently alongside, AT CLOSING? 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  gap_mitigated: If (and only if) you coded a structural gap above, was that gap
    documented as contractually absorbed at closing via a transitional-services or
    operating agreement allocating the shared substrate? yes / no / NA (NA if no gap).

E. collapse_state: Any Tier-1 fusion documented in the deal structure? none /
   T1=T4 (founder identity IS the product) / T1=T3 (the legal subject IS a specific
   natural person) / T1=T3=T4 / T1=T2 / T1=T6 / uncertain.

outcomes.

# Structural sub-dossier — Expeditors International of Washington, Inc. (closing-era structure)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. This sub-dossier describes ONLY the entity's
> structure as documented in the contemporaneous closing-era filing — what the drawn
> filing is and how the business was organized at that time. It contains no
> post-period outcome information.

## What the drawn filing is
- The drawn accession is a Form 8-K "Current Report," dated June 10, 2014 (date of
  earliest event reported), filed by Expeditors International of Washington, Inc. under
  Item 7.01 (Regulation FD Disclosure); it is a question-and-answer document responding
  to "SELECTED INQUIRIES RECEIVED THROUGH JUNE 9, 2014" from shareholders, not a merger
  agreement, tender offer, or deal-terms document. [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]
- No discrete acquisition, merger, spin-off, or asset transfer is executed or documented
  in the drawn filing; it references, but does not effectuate, any transaction. [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]
- The report is signed by Jeffrey S. Musser (President, Chief Executive Officer and
  Director) and R. Jordan Gates (President and Chief Operating Officer). [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]

## Controlling intent / imprint at the time
- The filing states a "newly appointed President and CEO, Jeff Musser," and describes a
  "strategic assessment" then underway framed as "as much about what will not change as
  it is about what we will change and at the top of the things that will not change is
  our culture." [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]
- Senior management describes the company's culture as what "defines" the firm and is
  "completely responsible" for how it "got to be what we are." [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]
- The filing describes Peter J. Rose as a "retiring founder" and 25-year CEO awarded an
  ~$8 million retirement bonus stated to be borne "by management, not by the
  shareholders" and paid "from an executive bonus pool formula" in effect since the
  company began trading publicly. [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]

## Business / value-capture model and the product
- The business is a freight-forwarding / global logistics operation; the customer-facing
  service is freight consolidation and forwarding (airfreight, ocean, and an
  intra-continental "Transcon" time-definite service). [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]
- The entity uses independent agents in markets that will not "sustain one of our
  offices"; its 2013 Form 10-K is stated to report "relationships with 44 independent
  agents," and agent economics run on "a variable model" where "We split net freight
  profits with each other and each pay for their own respective cost of operations." [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]

## How units are added to the organization (people/process/product alignment)
- When the entity opens its own office it "typically approach[es] our existing agent and
  try to have a discussion about purchasing them or barring that at least forming a joint
  venture," and "In the preponderance of the cases, we have acquired the agent outright
  on a deferred payout basis." [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]
- On converting an agency into a company office the entity assumes "all the
  responsibilities, financial and otherwise, of financing that office," so the acquired
  local operation is folded into the entity's own offices rather than run at arm's
  length. [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]
- Management characterizes such additions as happening "in an evolutionary manner" and
  "naturally," and frames future growth as being in "optimizing our existing network,
  augmenting it with naturally evolving agent acquisition opportunities as they present
  themselves," rather than in a program of consolidating acquisitions. [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]

## Other contemporaneous structural facts stated in the filing
- The filing states the proxy statement reports the company has "14,000 employees," of
  whom "5,172 employees enrolled in our Employee Stock Purchase Plan" as of the
  2013-2014 offering. [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]
- The filing states, as to the 2013 Annual Report balance sheet (page F-3), "we do not
  have any long-term debt." [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]
- The entity owns and occupies its Seattle headquarters ("215,000 square feet on 13
  stories"), of which it is "the largest tenant with over 210,000 square feet." [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]
- No transitional-services, shared-services, or supply agreement bridging a transferred
  substrate is present, because no discrete transfer of a business between owners is
  documented in the drawn filing. [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]

## Structural summary (closing-era only)
- The drawn filing is a Regulation FD investor-relations Q&A, not a deal-terms document;
  it documents no discrete acquisition. The contemporaneous structure is a non-asset,
  variable-margin freight-forwarding network that grows predominantly by internal office
  development, occasionally purchasing individual local agents outright (deferred payout)
  or via joint venture and folding them into wholly operated company offices, under a
  founder-imprinted culture the newly appointed CEO commits to preserving, and with no
  long-term debt. [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]

[SLICE END]

# Structural sub-dossier — Expeditors International of Washington, Inc. (closing-era structure)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written

## What the drawn filing is
- The drawn accession is a Form 8-K "Current Report," dated June 10, 2014 (date of
  earliest event reported), filed by Expeditors International of Washington, Inc. under
  Item 7.01 (Regulation FD Disclosure); it is a question-and-answer document responding
  to "SELECTED INQUIRIES RECEIVED THROUGH JUNE 9, 2014" from shareholders, not a merger
  agreement, tender offer, or deal-terms document. [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]
- No discrete acquisition, merger, spin-off, or asset transfer is executed or documented
  in the drawn filing; it references, but does not effectuate, any transaction. [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]
- The report is signed by Jeffrey S. Musser (President, Chief Executive Officer and
  Director) and R. Jordan Gates (President and Chief Operating Officer). [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]

## Controlling intent / imprint at the time
- The filing states a "newly appointed President and CEO, Jeff Musser," and describes a
  "strategic assessment" then underway framed as "as much about what will not change as
  it is about what we will change and at the top of the things that will not change is
  our culture." [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]
- Senior management describes the company's culture as what "defines" the firm and is
  "completely responsible" for how it "got to be what we are." [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]
- The filing describes Peter J. Rose as a "retiring founder" and 25-year CEO awarded an
  ~$8 million retirement bonus stated to be borne "by management, not by the
  shareholders" and paid "from an executive bonus pool formula" in effect since the
  company began trading publicly. [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]

## Business / value-capture model and the product
- The business is a freight-forwarding / global logistics operation; the customer-facing
  service is freight consolidation and forwarding (airfreight, ocean, and an
  intra-continental "Transcon" time-definite service). [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]
- The entity uses independent agents in markets that will not "sustain one of our
  offices"; its 2013 Form 10-K is stated to report "relationships with 44 independent
  agents," and agent economics run on "a variable model" where "We split net freight
  profits with each other and each pay for their own respective cost of operations." [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]

## How units are added to the organization (people/process/product alignment)
- When the entity opens its own office it "typically approach[es] our existing agent and
  try to have a discussion about purchasing them or barring that at least forming a joint
  venture," and "In the preponderance of the cases, we have acquired the agent outright
  on a deferred payout basis." [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]
- On converting an agency into a company office the entity assumes "all the
  responsibilities, financial and otherwise, of financing that office," so the acquired
  local operation is folded into the entity's own offices rather than run at arm's
  length. [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]
- Management characterizes such additions as happening "in an evolutionary manner" and
  "naturally," and frames future growth as being in "optimizing our existing network,
  augmenting it with naturally evolving agent acquisition opportunities as they present
  themselves," rather than in a program of consolidating acquisitions. [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]

## Other contemporaneous structural facts stated in the filing
- The filing states the proxy statement reports the company has "14,000 employees," of
  whom "5,172 employees enrolled in our Employee Stock Purchase Plan" as of the
  2013-2014 offering. [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]
- The filing states, as to the 2013 Annual Report balance sheet (page F-3), "we do not
  have any long-term debt." [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]
- The entity owns and occupies its Seattle headquarters ("215,000 square feet on 13
  stories"), of which it is "the largest tenant with over 210,000 square feet." [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]
- No transitional-services, shared-services, or supply agreement bridging a transferred
  substrate is present, because no discrete transfer of a business between owners is
  documented in the drawn filing. [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]

## Structural summary (closing-era only)
- The drawn filing is a Regulation FD investor-relations Q&A, not a deal-terms document;
  it documents no discrete acquisition. The contemporaneous structure is a non-asset,
  variable-margin freight-forwarding network that grows predominantly by internal office
  development, occasionally purchasing individual local agents outright (deferred payout)
  or via joint venture and folding them into wholly operated company offices, under a
  founder-imprinted culture the newly appointed CEO commits to preserving, and with no
  long-term debt. [SRC: SEC accession 0000746515-14-000023, Form 8-K Item 7.01]
